note: No DID class. The VTA never infers one — from a template, a context or a path — because a DID belongs to one class for its life (VTI-KEY-193), and a guessed `service` would make a person's identifier a node's. Absent is refused, not defaulted.
An integration class. 0.1 spoke of integration DIDs; an integration's identity is a service DID (VTI-KEY-192), so the class is `service` and there is no fourth value.

No hosting server. A did:webs DID is hosted only — the VTA has no inbound surface to serve one from — so there is no serverless form, and a request without `serverId` must fail validation rather than fall back to one.

The path carries the AID. The caller cannot know the AID — it is the digest of an inception event the VTA has not yet written — and the slot grammar is lowercase, so a case-sensitive AID segment is refused rather than taken as a path the VTA then appends a second AID to.
Caller-supplied key material. The VTA derives every key, with or without a template; a request naming a signing key is a request to custody a key the caller chose, and the closed schema refuses it.
A template and explicit services together. Two sources for one document would leave the operator unable to tell which shaped it, so they are exclusive rather than merged (CONVENTIONS.md §9.3).
A template and explicit aliases together. The template's `alsoKnownAs` is the alias list; an explicit one beside it is a second source.
Template variables without a template. Nothing would render them, so a request carrying them has asked for something the VTA cannot do.
A template scope without a template.
A template name outside the template grammar. Names are lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; anything else names no template in any scope.
A service id that is not a fragment. Ids are relative to the DID; an absolute id could name another DID's service.
A response without the DID's class. The class is fixed at creation and decides what the DID may later be adopted as; a response that omits it leaves the caller to guess.
